attributes.readMe:
## Warehouse (Lo)

Three kinds of location on one card, on purpose: a building you own, a 3PL that holds your stock, and a **virtual dropship location** that holds nothing at all but exists so an order can be allocated somewhere. Treating them as one card is what keeps allocation logic in one place.

Bin-level granularity is optional. A spare-room operation has no bins and reports no utilisation, rather than a fake 0%.

Coordinates are stored as a plain latitude/longitude pair rather than a geo field, so the card stays usable in realms that do not carry the catalog's geo blocks. A map consumer reads the pair.

### Example

Three warehouses: the Bermondsey arch (owned, 92% full), Trafford (3PL), and WidgetCo Direct (virtual — its isolated view explains that stock is never counted there).

### Non-goals

No slotting or bin optimisation. Bins are recorded, not arranged; `pick-list` sorts a route from bin labels and says why that is a property of the labelling rather than a solver.
